scenes.headline: How Breeze TTS 2 turns text into sound tokens
scenes.sub: A Gemma encoder, a Qwen3 backbone and a small depth decoder.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Salsa! Breeze TTS 2 is an open-weight speech model making two hundred sound tokens a second. Here's how.

scenes.label: The trick
scenes.text: Each 80 ms frame is 16 codebooks deep. The big backbone picks only the first; a small depth decoder fills in the other 15.
scenes.say: Each frame is sixteen codebooks deep. The big backbone picks only the first; a small depth decoder fills in the other fifteen.

scenes.title: From text to 80 ms of audio

steps.say: Your text goes through a Gemma encoder. It's bidirectional, so it needs the whole sentence first.
Its output is projected into the backbone, Qwen3's layer stack, which samples codebook zero.
A twelve-layer depth decoder takes its hidden state and returns codebooks one to fifteen.
A causal codec decoder turns the sixteen codes into eighty milliseconds of audio, with no lookahead.

steps.label: 16 codebooks x 12.5 frames: 200 tokens a second
steps.say: Sixteen codebooks, twelve and a half frames a second: two hundred tokens per second of speech.

steps.label: Row 0: the backbone. Rows 1-15: a model 3.2x smaller
steps.say: Only the top row touches the big backbone. The rest go through a model three point two times smaller.

scenes.title: Layer evaluations per 80 ms frame
scenes.note: the fifteen-step depth loop is captured as one CUDA graph
scenes.say: But the small one runs fifteen times a frame, a hundred and eighty layer steps to twenty-eight. So its loop is one CUDA graph.

scenes.title: Guidance that keeps the voice
scenes.say: Voice cloning is just a prompt. Guidance then steers the delivery.

parts.note: positive branch: the reference plus the instruction
parts.say: Positive: the reference plus your instruction.

parts.note: negative branch: the same reference, no instruction

parts.say: Scale the gap, and only the instruction grows.

scenes.label: time to first audio at p50, on the company's own hosted benchmark
scenes.note: the README's under 40 ms starts its clock after the text encoder
scenes.say: One caveat: the README's forty milliseconds skips the text encoder. The company's hosted benchmark says one hundred thirty-three point six.

scenes.text: Split the frame: a big model for one codebook, a small one for fifteen, and a codec that never waits.
scenes.say: Split the frame: a big model for one codebook, a small one for fifteen, and a codec that never waits.

recap: Gemma reads the text; Qwen3 picks codebook 0
A 12-layer depth decoder fills in 15 more
scenes.say: To recap: Gemma reads, Qwen3 picks one codebook, a small decoder fills fifteen, and guidance amplifies the instruction.
